description:
FOUND s465ba (Opus, round 23) while probing #1032.  PRE-EXISTING: verified
byte-identical on a 1fed80b worktree for the PATH and LEXICAL spellings (the
bareword spelling could not be measured there â it was #1032's crash).

REPRO (scratch/p14-stat-scalar.pl):

    open(my $fh, '<', '/etc/passwd') or die;
    print "1 ", scalar(stat($fh)), "\n";
    print "2 ", scalar(stat("/etc/passwd")), "\n";
    print "3 ", scalar(stat("/no/such/xyz")), "\n";
    print "4 ", scalar(lstat("/etc/passwd")), "\n";
    my $n = stat("/etc/passwd");
    print "5 ", $n, "\n";
    print "6 ", (stat("/etc/passwd") ? "true" : "false"), "\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  1  1  (empty)  1  1     true
  PCL:          1  66306145495743318810002958178838287717625828811762582
                   88140966  (the same digit soup)  (empty)  (soup)
                   ARRAY(0x1)                              true

So THREE of the six diverge and three agree: the FAILURE answer ("" for a
missing file) is right, and so is truthiness, because a non-empty list is
true either way.  What is wrong is the VALUE: perl's `pp_stat` pushes
`&PL_sv_yes` in scalar context, PCL hands back the 13-element vector, which
`scalar()` then stringifies by concatenating its elements and `my $n =`
stores as an array reference.

WHY IT MATTERS: `stat` in scalar context is the ordinary "did it work" test
(`stat($f) or die`), and the ordinary spelling is safe by accident because
truthiness agrees.  The two that are NOT safe are `my $ok = stat($f)`
(perl 1, PCL an ARRAY ref, so `$ok == 1` is an address comparison) and any
`print`/interpolation of it.

FIX SHAPE (untried): `p-stat` / `p-lstat` are wantarray-INSENSITIVE today.
They need the `*wantarray*` protocol like the other list-or-scalar builtins:
list context â the 13-element list; scalar/void â 1 on success and "" on
failure (perl's `PL_sv_yes` / `PL_sv_no`, NOT undef â `defined(scalar stat
"/no/such")` is TRUE in perl, probed).  Check the same question for the
family that shares `%p-stat-arg`: the filetests already answer a scalar, and
`-s` answers a size, so `stat`/`lstat` are the two.  NB `%WANTARRAY_SENSITIVE`
(the compiler's table of context-sensitive builtins) must gain them or the
context wrap will not be emitted.

NO ROW COST MEASURED: the sweep and the op/ companion are clean with it, so
nothing currently asserts the scalar form.

=== DONE (s470bx, 2026-09-06) ===

FIXED in the two edits the task named, plus one the task did not: the answer
itself is now ONE function, `%p-stat-answer`, because `stat` and `lstat`
differ only in which syscall filled the buffer (rule 11).

  * `%WANTARRAY_SENSITIVE` in `Pl/ExprToCL.pm` gains `stat lstat`, so every
    call site binds *wantarray* to its own STATIC context and the enclosing
    sub's cannot leak in.  A tail-position `return stat $f` keeps INHERIT_CTX
    and therefore answers the CALLER's context, which is perl's rule.
  * `%p-stat-answer` gives the 13-element list in LIST context and perl's
    &PL_sv_yes / &PL_sv_no otherwise â 1, or the EMPTY STRING (not undef, so
    `defined(scalar stat "/no/such")` is TRUE, as the task said).

PROBED, 24 rows over every context the task named plus a few it did not
(scratch/s470bx/p1043.pl): `my $x =`, `if()`, `or die`, `scalar()`, `my @s =`,
`my ($dev) =`, `scalar(()=)`, string interpolation, a sub called in list and
in scalar context, `stat _` after a success and after a failure, void context,
a lexical-handle operand, and numeric/string use of the answer.  Byte-identical
to perl 5.40.3; TWELVE of the 24 differ on the fcf076f1 tree.

ROWS: t/op/stat_errors.t 510/128 -> 532/106.  Its assertion is
`is $res, $op =~ /\A-/ ? undef : !!0` â for the two non-filetest ops it wants
&PL_sv_no exactly.  22 rows, all `result of stat|lstat <arg>`, removed from
`baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv` BY HAND with the cause.

BARS: generation v2-840, three artifacts regenerated (their diff is the gen
stamp and nothing else); corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files, SILENT-DROP 5
unchanged; emission-ab over lib + perl's t/ + cpan-tests (1035 files) SAME
1030 / DIFF 5 / RCDIFF 0, and every one of the five diffs is exactly
`(p-stat X)` -> `(p-scalar-ctx (p-stat X))`; ir-host-leak 31 leaks over 111,
byte-identical to the base; full sweep GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed, drops 5 =
census, TOTAL passing 18647 (+0).

GUARD: `Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t` rows 72-85 (x2 emission paths), values
taken from the SAME program under perl.  Inverse-verified: 16 of the 28 fail
on a fcf076f1 extraction â the LIST and truthiness rows pass on BOTH trees,
which is the point (truthiness always agreed, which is why nothing caught
this).  `Pl/t/fileio-01.t`'s three transpile-SHAPE rows now assert the wrap
itself (s377 rule: the edit STRENGTHENS the claim).

FILED #1290 from a probe of the emission A/B's fifth mover: `\FUNC(...)` does
not spread over the returned LIST (`my @r = \stat($Curdir)` is 1 ref, perl
says 13).  PRE-EXISTING â `\localtime(0)` already answered 1 ref on the base
tree â and independent of this change.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, every operand spelling): `stat` / `lstat` in SCALAR context answer the 13-element LIST instead of perl's 1-or-"" success flag -- `scalar(stat($file))` is 1 in perl and 6630614549574331881000295817883828771762582881176258288140966 in PCL, and `my $n = stat($file)` is 1 in perl and `ARRAY(0x1)` in PCL.
